items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And then a guy from Ann Arbor, Ron Brooks submitted some music

ctx.x: No, well I was working with a cadre of musicians. I was working with Phil Ranelin, which we started a partnership, Tribe Records. The magazine was different. But I needed some help on administrative stuff so I incorporated with Phil and myself as Tribe Records. And then Marcus — I used Marcus Belgrave and Harold McKinney basically was the network. Because we was playing in each other’s group. I was playing in Marcus’s group, me and Phil was playing in Marcus’s group, was playing in Harold’s group, you know, and…

groove. And then a guy from Ann Arbor, Ron Brooks submitted some music and David Durrah out of Cleveland submitted some music. So anyway that’s how that started, and then we distributed this music by independent distributors that was happening all over America, independent distributors, they wanted to distribute their own product and have their own catalogue as opposed to working for Atlantic Records or a big corporation. This was like an independent revolution as it were, you know, in the 60s. Everybody was…
Yeah. Sort of like saying, “Oh I can’t blame my bad saxophone playing on my reed anymore.”
